releases.name: tasteskill v2.5.1
releases.body:
What a 44-site test of 2.5.0 showed, fixed: builds now iterate until the checker is clean, every page moves, products without photographs are shown in photographs, palettes fit the trade, the copy gets a voice of its own, and nothing lies on anything else on a phone. The install name did not change.

- **A finish gate:** `scripts/gate.mjs` runs the checker, the layout check and a copy lint, and a build is not done until its last line reads `GATE: PASS` (three rounds, five waivers with reasons at most). In Claude Code it runs as a Stop hook from the skill itself. It never traps an agent: a question to the user costs no round, and `gate.mjs --done` ends a build at the user's word.
- **Motion on every page:** every hero enters once on load, and every page carries one or two scroll moments. Cafes, shops and services get photo- and type-led ones (new `photo-chapters`, a film look for `picture-develops`); shader effects stay on tech pages.
- **Photographs over renders:** a product without the client's pictures is shown in licensed stand-in photographs (`photos.mjs search`: Wikimedia Commons, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA and public domain only). A 3D render only when the brief asks for one.

releases.name: tasteskill v2.5
releases.body:
A complete rebuild of `design-taste-frontend` around professional company websites at the figma.com and x.ai bar. The install name did not change.

- **One page system:** every build starts from the same starter. The hero fills the first screen, one section per screen, equal left and right edges.
- **Effects only where they fit:** shader grounds, scroll moments and big scenes only on software, tech and gaming pages. Cafes, shops, hotels and services get real photographs and no effects.
- **Real product UI:** 19 HTML UI fragments (chat, diff review, terminal, pipeline board, voice and more), and a software page shows its product in one app window.
- **Real photographs and icons:** vetted Unsplash and Wikimedia Commons frames by trade, no captions, one footer credit line; real brand icons, never drawn.
- **No two pages alike:** the hero layout, palette, type pairing and ground are dealt at random.
- **A product is always shown, and big:** with no photographs it is rendered from a spec of its parts, and the colour buttons change the picture.
- **Checked in a real browser:** over 100 checks at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390. A page with a FAIL is not done.

releases.name: tasteskill v2.1.5
releases.body:
Fixes from the community. Thanks to everyone who reported and sent them.

- **Safe text in charts and split headings** (#160, #169, thanks @jcastilla89 and @Pablolakotek): `charts.js` and the `Stage.split` fallback escape the text they insert, so a label or heading from user data can no longer inject markup.
- **No lost screenshots when two widths share a class** (#162, #165, thanks @nosawavey-spec and @ketpatil77).
- **Keyboard and accessible names** (#170, thanks @MrBinnacle): every control works from the keyboard and has an accessible name.
- **The italic faces load** (#161, fix from #166, thanks @nosawavey-spec and @ketpatil77): Boska, Erode and Sentient request their italic weight.
- **`edge-text` no longer fails ellipsised lines** (#156, thanks @shoctroper).
- **Inspect the production build** (#171, thanks @lilozzy): the Gate says so, and the inspector warns when it is looking at a dev server.
- **The redraw rule names its third reason** (#163, thanks @Tsury).
- CI also checks that every text file is clean UTF-8.

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"
```

Claude Code plugin users: `/plugin update`.

releases.name: tasteskill v2.1.4
releases.body:
This release makes the inspector's browser profiles safe when several runs go at once ([#157](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/issues/157), [#158](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/158), [#159](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/pull/159)). The rules of `design-taste-frontend` are unchanged; only `scripts/lib/cdp.mjs` changed.

- **Fix: one inspector run could delete the browser profile of another run that was still going.** Chrome keeps no `lockfile` on macOS and Linux, so the sweep added in 2.1.0 judged a profile unused by its age alone. A second run started during a long one could then pull that run's profile away. Thanks to @t4sh for the report and the fix.
- **Leftover profiles are cleaned up again, safely.** Every profile now carries `taste-skill-owner.json` with the machine and the process IDs of the run and its Chrome. A later run removes a profile left by a killed run only when that file names this machine and neither process is alive. A profile without the file is never touched.

Profiles left by earlier versions are not removed automatically. To clear them, delete the `ad-chrome-*` folders in your temp folder (or in `TASTE_SKILL_TMP`).

Update:

``

**Taste Skill** (`tasteskill 2.5.1`) is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents build professional company websites at the `figma.com` and `x.ai` level instead of assembling a generic landing page. Every build uses plain copy, one design system, one section per screen, equal left and right edges, real photographs (licensed stand-ins when the client has none), real brand icons and real product UI, a hero entrance and one or two dealt moments on every page, quiet micro-interactions, and shader effects and scroll scenes kept strictly for tech, gaming and software pages, all verified in a real browser by a checker and a finish gate that enforce the rules. Pages built from a single brief in earlier v2 runs:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0). ## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` That installs the skill with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. The skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium** (set `CHROME_PATH` if it is in a non-standard place). Optional: **ffmpeg** on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in `photos.mjs`. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so it does not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skill into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates it in place. On Windows (Git Bash) it makes a real link, or a directory junction when symlinks are not allowed, and it reports an older copied folder instead of skipping it silently.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See [Moved skills](#moved-skills). ## How 2.5 works Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies `assets/` into the project, starts from `assets/starter.html` and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business (`software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service` or `place`) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup: 1. **Deal tokens and layout.** `scripts/start.mjs` deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind (`library/palettes.json`, `library/type.json`), and `assets/layout/deal.mjs` deals a hero layout (`split`, `centred`, `product`, `photo`, `place`, `collage`, `editorial`, `word`, `film`, `statement` or `triptych`). 2. **Start from one system.** `assets/starter.html`, `assets/system.css` and `assets/layout/layout.css` enforce one section per screen at desktop (`1440x900`), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer (`footer.closing`). 3. **Show real product UI and real photographs.** Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards (`assets/ui/cards.css`) with rewritten HTML UI fragments (`assets/ui/`) and node-and-line diagrams (`assets/diagrams/`), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by `scripts/icons.mjs`. Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs (`scripts/photos.mjs`, `assets/photos/`), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images. 4. **Keep effects for tech and gaming pages.** Shader grounds (`scripts/effects.mjs`), scroll scenes (`assets/scenes/`) and procedural 3D prints (`assets/objects/`) are dealt only on `software`, `tech` and `gaming` pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion. Every page gets a hero entrance and one or two moments from `scripts/moments.mjs`; cafes, hotels, shops, studios and services get only the photo- and type-led ones, and zero WebGL. 5. **Check in a real browser over HTTP.** `scripts/consistency.mjs`, `assets/layout/check.mjs`, `scripts/perf.mjs` and `scripts/shoot.mjs` render the built page in headless Chrome across `1440`, `1024`, `768` and `390`, catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. `scripts/gate.mjs` then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most. Details of what changed from `2.1.x` are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## The tools Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything. | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `scripts/start.mjs` | Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the `` links and `:root` tokens. | | `assets/layout/deal.mjs` | Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; `assets/layout/check.mjs` checks it with long-headline stress tests. | | `scripts/photos.mjs` | Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line. | | `scripts/icons.mjs` | Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files. | | `scripts/effects.mjs`, `scripts/moments.mjs` | Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind. | | `scripts/gate.mjs`, `scripts/copy-lint.mjs` | The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs. | | `scripts/consistency.mjs` | The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at `1440`, `1024`, `820`, `768` and `390` and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule. | | `scripts/perf.mjs`, `scripts/shoot.mjs` | Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots. | First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): `node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software` (kinds: `software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service`, `place`). The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill (credits). Watch the launch film.

Install

npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend"

That installs the skill with the npx skills CLI.

The skill runs its scripts with Node 22+ and an installed Chrome, Edge or Chromium (set CHROME_PATH if it is in a non-standard place). Optional: ffmpeg on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in photos.mjs. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.

Claude Code plugin

Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under taste-skill:, so it does not collide with your other skills.

/plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill

Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See Moved skills.

How 2.5 works

Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies assets/ into the project, starts from assets/starter.html and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business (software, gaming, tech, product, service or place) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup:

  1. Deal tokens and layout. scripts/start.mjs deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind (library/palettes.json, library/type.json), and assets/layout/deal.mjs deals a hero layout (split, centred, product, photo, place, collage, editorial, word, film, statement or triptych).
  2. Start from one system. assets/starter.html, assets/system.css and assets/layout/layout.css enforce one section per screen at desktop (1440x900), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer (footer.closing).
  3. Show real product UI and real photographs. Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards (assets/ui/cards.css) with rewritten HTML UI fragments (assets/ui/) and node-and-line diagrams (assets/diagrams/), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by scripts/icons.mjs. Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs (scripts/photos.mjs, assets/photos/), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images.
  4. Keep effects for tech and gaming pages. Shader grounds (scripts/effects.mjs), scroll scenes (assets/scenes/) and procedural 3D prints (assets/objects/) are dealt only on software, tech and gaming pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion.   5. Check in a real browser over HTTP. scripts/consistency.mjs, assets/layout/check.mjs, scripts/perf.mjs and scripts/shoot.mjs render the built page in headless Chrome across 1440, 1024, 768 and 390, catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. scripts/gate.mjs then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most.

Details of what changed from 2.1.x are in the changelog.

The tools

Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything.

Tool What it does
scripts/start.mjs Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the <head> links and :root tokens.
assets/layout/deal.mjs Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; assets/layout/check.mjs checks it with long-headline stress tests.
scripts/photos.mjs Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line.
scripts/icons.mjs Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files.
scripts/effects.mjs, scripts/moments.mjs Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind.
scripts/gate.mjs, scripts/copy-lint.mjs The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs.
scripts/consistency.mjs The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at 1440, 1024, 820, 768 and 390 and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule.
scripts/perf.mjs, scripts/shoot.mjs Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots.

First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software (kinds: software, gaming, tech, product, service, place). Check a built page with node scripts/consistency.mjs <url or file> --page <kind>.

Moved skills

This repo holds one skill, design-taste-frontend. The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names:

Install name Where it lives now
high-end-visual-design, minimalist-ui, industrial-brutalist-ui, gpt-taste, stitch-design-taste, design-taste-frontend-v1, design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics
imagegen-frontend-web, imagegen-frontend-mobile, brandkit, image-to-code Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills
redesign-existing-projects Part of design-taste-frontend, which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything
full-output-enforcement Removed. For the same problem, see Leonxlnx/unlazy

Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name:

npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill "high-end-visual-design"

Common Questions

What does the skill need?
Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional (WebP photographs and the phone crop of a hero photograph). It installs nothing and uses no API keys. Bundled Commons photographs are stored locally; network access is used only when downloading additional photographs, Google Fonts or brand icons.

Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?
From the skill's vetted photograph library (assets/photos/photos.json, including bundled Wikimedia Commons WebP sets and Unsplash photographs) dealt by scripts/photos.mjs. Library frames are used for trade and material details (or marked explicitly as draft stand-ins when the client has no photographs yet), never passed off as the client's own room, staff or product, and credited in one expandable footer line (photos.mjs credits).

Does it work with React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML?
An empty folder gets a static page from assets/starter.html. An existing React, Vue, Svelte, Astro or Tailwind project is built in its own stack, with the kit served from its public folder; a Next.js brief is built as a static export. The browser checks run on the served or built page.

When does a page get shaders or scroll effects?
Shaders only on software, tech (technical hardware) and gaming pages, and always within a four-context WebGL budget with static phone and reduced-motion fallbacks. Places, shops, cafes, hotels, studios, services and everyday physical products stay calm: photographs, sharp typography and flat colour, with a hero entrance and one or two photo- or type-led moments in their own sections.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An anti-slop frontend framework and skill set designed to prevent AI agents from generating generic, poorly designed UI.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Taste-Skill acts as an anti-slop frontend framework intended to elevate the design quality of code generated by AI agents. It addresses the common issue where LLMs produce generic, visually unappealing, or heavily boilerplate UIs by providing a curated set of design rules and constraints. The project functions as a specific 'skill' that can be injected into agentic workflows to guide styling, layout, and component choices. By enforcing strong design opinions and best practices, it ensures the resulting frontends look premium and bespoke rather than obviously machine-generated. It effectively gives the AI a sense of 'good taste' in modern web design.
keyFeatures: Anti-Slop Directives: Prevents the generation of generic, overused UI patterns and standard Bootstrap-style layouts.
Design Opinionation: Enforces strong, modern design principles regarding typography, spacing, and color palettes.
Agent Skill Integration: Designed to be easily consumed and executed by autonomous coding agents like Claude Code or Codex.
Premium Component Constraints: Guides the AI to use modern frontend techniques and minimalist aesthetics.
Framework Agnostic Concepts: Focuses on core design taste that can be applied across different web frameworks and libraries.

useCases.description: Generate wireframes and prototypes that are immediately presentable to stakeholders without requiring a manual design pass.

useCases.title: Low-code Customization
useCases.description: Enhance low-code platform generation capabilities by ensuring the raw output adheres to modern aesthetic standards.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Developers, designers, and 'vibecoders' who use AI tools to generate frontend code. It is for anyone frustrated by the generic, unpolished look of standard LLM-generated user interfaces.
